justification: Both pages use the same layout: a header band, then a short letter that fills only the top half of the page. B's body text is set in a tighter serif with normal word spacing. A's looser letter-spacing makes uneven gaps in the justified lines and breaks 'addition-al' awkwardly (A1). B's navy band is more restrained and professional than A's saturated bright blue. B's lines read more cleanly and its spacing is more even (B1).

Both pages use the same navy header band and the same content, with the lower half of the page left empty. A sets justified sans-serif body text with wide word gaps and hyphenation breaks ("Manage-ment", "ad-equate"), which looks uneven. B uses a serif at a comfortable line length with a more natural ragged right edge, so it reads more smoothly. B's bold subject line wraps and leaves a short orphan, which is a minor flaw. B is slightly better overall.

Design A and B share the same structure. A has a bold sans-serif title, but it carries a stray '1' numbering prefix ('1 Invoice INV-2025-0418') and a redundant running header that repeats the invoice number. Its justified text opens wide gaps in the Bill to line and the Payment line. B has a cleaner serif title with no stray number, a navy top band, and ragged-right text with even word spacing. B's table is slightly more spacious, and the footer is simple. The overall impression favours B, though A's bolder title has stronger hierarchy.

B's serif body is tighter, with normal word spacing and a bolder serif title on a calm navy band. A's text is letter-spaced and set wider, with uneven word gaps and an awkward hyphenated 'addition-al'. A's saturated blue band is louder and its text block is narrower and more cramped. Both leave the bottom half of the page empty, and B's even rhythm reads better.

A is a restrained serif invoice with a thin top rule and a title that sits comfortably above the table. B's heavy navy title block and a top band repeating the invoice number, which is repeated again in the footer, add redundancy on a one-page invoice. B's sans table is clean and legible, similar to A's, but A feels more refined and balanced.

B keeps one left margin: the title, address, table and payment text all align, and it has a strong top band. In A the title sits at a different left edge from the body text and table, which are indented, so the page looks misaligned. A's justified text also opens wide word gaps in the payment line and the Bill to line. B's serif title is less bold but sits more coherently with the body. Both tables are similar, and both pages leave the lower half empty.

A opens with a navy title band and gives each statement its own page, with consistent header and footer bands. Its tables are intact, and the shaded current-year column is clear. B splits the Statement of Financial Position across two pages, leaving a header row with no context at the top of B3. B also spends a mostly empty page on the cover, and its margins and indents are inconsistent: headings sit at a different left edge from the body and tables. B's serif numerals are small and less crisp than A's. A's hierarchy and rhythm are tighter, though A4 is sparse.

B reads as a cohesive, calm report: a full-bleed navy cover (B1), a consistent top rule on every page, an elegant serif throughout, and tables aligned with the text margin (B2-B4). A mixes a bold geometric sans heading with a serif body, and its headings hang left of the indented text and tables, so the left edge is ragged (A2, A4). A's tables start mid-page and split awkwardly (A2-A3), with a very short row-split on A2; B splits similarly but more neatly. A's plain white cover is weaker than B's. B's headings are lighter and slightly less prominent, which is a small cost.

A has a dark full-bleed cover (A1) and a top rule on every page, which gives it a more finished look. Its single serif family is consistent and its headings are well scaled. B mixes a geometric sans for headings with a serif for body text. B's section headings hang out into the left margin while the body and tables are indented (B2, B4), which makes the left edge misaligned. B also has an odd hyphenation ("Inter--segment") and uneven number alignment in its parenthesised columns (B2). A's tables are cleanly aligned, though A1 splits the financial position table across pages, as B does.

B has a navy title band and a header band that give a clear identity and a strong entry point (B1). Its sans-serif face is clean and consistent with the table. A uses a plain title with a stray '1' numbering prefix ('1 Invoice INV-2025-0418'), which repeats in the header and looks like an error (A1). A's serif body with a sans title is serviceable, but the bill-to and dates run together with justified spacing in both. B's tables are equally tidy, so the band treatment decides it.

A uses an elegant serif for the title and body, and the dark band gives the heading a refined look. Its justified text sets the address and subject on single lines. B uses a sans-serif title with a serif body, which feels less cohesive. In B the subject line wraps and leaves an orphaned '2026', and the address wraps to a second line with 'BA2 3QT' left alone. A reads slightly cleaner, though its justified text shows some hyphenation and loose spacing.

A sets the body in a serif with a comfortable measure and clear line spacing, and the bold subject line stands out. B uses a sans at small size with a wider measure, so lines run long and hyphenation breaks are more noticeable. Both share the same header band and leave the lower half of the page empty.

I lean toward B at low confidence, though A has real strengths. A has strong navy header and footer bands, a centred cover, and clear table rules (A2-A5). Its numbered headings are awkward, though: '4.1 1. Basis of preparation' double-numbers, and '4 Notes' is stranded. A also splits the statement of financial position awkwardly across pages, leaving only three rows on A2. B has a cleaner, more refined type pairing and tidy headings without double numbering (B4). Its tables are well aligned and the footers are quiet (B2-B3). B's weakness is the indented table and text against flush-left headings, plus the same page-split problem. A's bands give stronger structure, but B's cleaner heading logic and typography edge it out.

B puts the title band and income statement on one page, and its header and footer bands frame every page consistently. Each statement sits whole on its own page. A has a mostly empty cover. It also splits the Statement of Financial Position across two pages, repeating the header with a table that starts mid-section on A2 and continues on A3. Its table indents are inconsistent with the headings, and its pages are left sparse. B's tables are cleaner and carry the same column alignment from page to page.

A pairs a serif body with a bold sans title, which reads as more refined, and it has wider margins and looser line spacing. The recipient line wraps awkwardly but stays readable. B uses one sans family with a narrower measure and more tightly packed text, and its hyphenations are more visible. Both put a band at the top and leave the lower half of the page empty.

A pairs a restrained navy band with a refined serif title that suits a professional letter, and its body text is slightly tighter and more even. B's bright blue band and geometric sans title feel less formal, and its looser tracking leaves the bold subject line breaking awkwardly onto a second line with the orphan '2026'. Both leave the lower half of the page empty and have the same run-together address blocks.

A keeps consistent margins: the title rule, text and table share one left edge, and a navy band tops the page. In B the title and rule sit outdented from the indented body, and the table runs close to the right edge, which looks misaligned and unbalanced. B's justified text also leaves wide word gaps in the Bill to line and the payment line. A's serif typography is more cohesive and its table spacing is cleaner.

A has a clean serif title with a rule above it and a navy band at the top. Its margins are generous and its footer is minimal. B's title carries a stray '1' numbering prefix, and the running header repeats it, which is redundant clutter. B also mixes a sans title with serif body text, and its justified text leaves wide gaps in the Bill to line. The tables are nearly identical.

A has a strong navy title band and header bar, so the invoice title stands out clearly. The header repeats the invoice number, which is redundant with the title block. B is elegant and readable with a serif face, but its title is weak and plain, and the thin rules give less hierarchy. The tables are nearly identical, and both leave the lower half of the page empty.

B puts the title band on the same page as the income statement and adds running header and footer bands. Each statement sits whole on its own page. A spends a full dark cover page on the title, and its statement of financial position splits across A2 and A3, with the table header repeated mid-table. B's sans-serif tables are clean and easy to scan (B2). A's serif face looks elegant, but the split table and sparse page 5 hurt it.

The two pages have the same structure, so the difference is in the details. A uses a darker navy band that looks more professional for an accountancy letter. Its body text is tighter and more natural to read. B uses a bright blue band, and its letterspaced body text and wider tracking make the justified lines look looser and slightly less comfortable to read.

A has a navy title band and a running header band that give a clear entry point, and its content is aligned to one left edge. B's title sits outdented from the indented body, which looks misaligned, and its header is just a thin rule. The tables are nearly identical, and both leave the bottom half of the page empty. A also repeats the invoice number in the header band, which is redundant.

A uses bold sans headings with a blue title band on page 1, so the hierarchy is clear and the content starts immediately. B spends a full page on a mostly empty dark cover, and its light serif headings are barely bigger than body text. B's dark donut chart (B3) has even lower contrast on its labels than A's. Both have the same table and the same awkward line break in decision 1. A's page 1 flows from title to content and feels more complete.

A sets the letter in a serif face with more generous paragraph spacing and a larger band, which reads as a more formal letter of engagement. B's sans-serif body is serviceable but tighter and more generic, with slightly cramped spacing. Both share the same structure and the same large empty lower half.

A uses one elegant serif family with a dark full-bleed cover (A1) and a clean hierarchy. Its note headings are consistent and its footers are minimal (A2-A5). B mixes a sans heading face with serif body text. Its auto-numbering is awkward and redundant ("4.1 1. Basis of preparation", "4.4 17. Borrowings", B4-B5), and the heavy header and footer bands add clutter (B2-B5). B's cover is plain and centred, which is fine but less striking. Tables are similar in both, though A's are slightly more refined.

B has a strong navy title band and a header strip, so the invoice title stands out immediately. Its table is cleanly aligned with a consistent left margin. A's heading sits outdented from the indented body, which looks misaligned, and its justified text leaves wide word gaps. B's header strip repeats the invoice number redundantly, and its justified text also has some gaps, but overall it is more polished.

A has cleaner headings with no clumsy auto-numbering. B adds redundant numbering such as '4.1 1. Basis of preparation' and '4.4 17. Borrowings', which is confusing and clutters the hierarchy (B4, B5). B's heavy navy header and footer bands do give clear navigation, but they are dense and repeat the document title on every page (B2). A's quiet running footers keep the pages calmer. The table styling is nearly identical in both. A's left-aligned cover title also feels more designed than B's centred one (A1).

A opens with a strong navy title band and gives each statement its own clean page. The balance sheet stays whole on A2 and the header and footer bands are clear. B splits the balance sheet across B2 and B3, repeating the table header mid-statement. B also has awkward numbering ("4.1 1. Basis of preparation", "4.4 17. Borrowings"), a mostly empty cover page, and a hyphenation glitch ("Inter- -segment"). A's headings are cleaner.

Both are the same letter with a header band and a large empty lower half. B uses a serif face, a taller band and wider margins. Its text is left-aligned with fewer awkward breaks, and it reads like a formal letter. A is justified sans-serif with loose word spacing and hyphenation (Manage-ment, ad-equate), which hurts the rhythm. A's band is slightly tighter, and its bold heading is a little stronger.

A has a dark cover page and a serif-only type system that feels cohesive and executive. Its donut chart has dark segments with unreadable dark labels (A3), and the chart title overlaps the ring. B has a saturated blue header band and mixes sans headings with serif body, so the headings sit at the margin while the body is indented. This looks less refined, though B's lighter blue donut keeps its labels more legible (B2). B packs everything into 3 pages, which is efficient, but A's cover and consistent restraint make it the more polished document.

Both are near-identical letters with a dark header band and a large empty lower half. A uses a bolder sans-serif title and a larger body size with a shorter line length, so it reads more easily. B has a smaller, tighter serif body with longer lines, and its address line runs the full width. A's bright navy band is also somewhat more distinct. A's subject line wraps awkwardly, but that is minor.

A keeps a consistent left margin, with the title, body and table aligned within symmetric margins, and it has a running header and a 'Page 1 of 1' footer. In B the title hangs out to the left of the indented body text, and the rule above it runs off-center. B's table also sits close to the right edge, so the page looks lopsided. The typography is similar in both, but A's title carries a stray '1' prefix that B avoids.

B reads as the cleaner, more finished document. Its serif typography is consistent, and its headings are free of the odd numbering in A ("4.1 1. Basis of preparation", "4.4 17. Borrowings"). Its cover is a full dark page with a left-aligned title, which looks more deliberate than A's small centred title on white (A1, B1). Its running footer is quiet and its rules are thin (B2-B5). The tables in both are similar, but B splits the statement of financial position at a more sensible point, and A's repeated header bands add heaviness (A2, A3). A's dark header and footer bands are stronger and give clear navigation, yet the confusing double numbering and running-header mismatch (A4 shows '4.1 1. Basis of preparation' on a page that opens with segment information) count against it.

B keeps the statement of financial position whole on one page (B2), while A splits it across pages 2 and 3 and repeats the header row (A2, A3). A also has a mostly empty cover page (A1) and clumsy heading numbering such as '4.1 1. Basis of preparation' (A4), whereas B uses clean note numbers (B3). B's navy title band on the first page is stronger and more compact (B1). Both end with a sparse last page.

A keeps each statement whole on its own page: the income statement sits under a strong navy title band on A1, and the financial position table is intact on A2. Running header and footer bands aid navigation. B splits the financial position table across B2 and B3, repeating the header row and leaving a stranded two-row fragment. B also spends a page on a mostly empty dark cover with little content. B's serif type is elegant, but its table numerals are less crisp than A's sans.

A has a clean title, with a rule above it and the page number in the footer. The title is outdented slightly from the indented body, which looks a little odd but is still tidy. B numbers its title "1 Invoice", which is a stray artifact. B also repeats the document title in the header and footer, and its header shows "1 Invoice INV-2025-0418" as redundant clutter. The tables are almost identical.

Both are nearly identical letters with a header band and a blank lower half. B's serif body with wider margins and a bolder band reads more like a formal letter. A's sans text is justified with more hyphenation (Manage-ment, ad-equate), and its tighter margins and wide word gaps hurt readability. B hyphenates too (addition-al) and leaves a widowed 'BA2 3QT' line, but overall it is slightly smoother.

A has a strong navy title band and a running header band that give a clear focal point. Its sans-serif table is clean with a distinct total row. B's title is a plain "1 Invoice" with a stray section number, and its serif body is weaker in hierarchy. Both have justified text that spaces the bill-to line unevenly, and both leave the lower half of the page empty. A's header text is repeated, but that is a minor flaw.
